# Independent raster corpus

Synthetic coordinate/color/alpha patterns authored for Rrrah and dedicated to
CC0. Generated with Pillow 12.3.0 by `scripts/generate-raster-fixtures.py`.
No third-party photographs or assets are included. Each `.rgba` oracle is the
independent Pillow decoder's row-major straight RGBA8 output. JPEG allows two
sample levels for decoder rounding; lossless formats require exact equality.
The manifest records file name, dimensions, tolerance, oracle, and source SHA256.
This is baseline pixel qualification, not a complete format variant corpus.

Sun Raster fixtures are generated by `scripts/generate-sun-fixtures.py`; their RGBA oracles come from Pillow. These include odd-width row padding, BGR/RGB, byte RLE, palette and monochrome.

The odd-width Sun RLE oracle comes from FFmpeg, checked against the source pattern: Pillow skips the encoded row-padding byte and shifts the following row. FFmpeg is used only for fixture verification, never runtime decoding.

Sun 32-bit XRGB/XBGR and RLE fixtures use FFmpeg oracles validated against the source RGB pattern. The leading X byte varies and must never become alpha.

DDS BC1/BC2/BC3 fixtures are hand-authored by `scripts/generate-dds-fixtures.py`, decoded independently by Pillow, with one level of interpolation rounding tolerance. BC1 includes a transparent-block case.

Uncompressed DDS RGB565/RGB24/BGRA32 oracles come from FFmpeg. RGB565 has odd-width pitch padding; BGRA includes transparent and partial-alpha pixels.

FFmpeg and Pillow ignore the legacy DDS pitch field. The padded RGB565 fixture uses an equivalent tightly packed DDS for the independent color oracle, while Rrrah decodes the padded source.

Six DX10 DDS fixtures cover RGBA8/BGRA8/BGRX8 UNORM and SRGB; RGBA8 oracles come from Pillow and BGRA/BGRX from FFmpeg; Rust tests separately verify transfer metadata and opaque BGRX alpha.

FFmpeg swaps R/B when decoding the DX10 RGBA8 fixtures on this runtime; Pillow matches the source pattern and is the oracle for formats 28/29.

BGRA/BGRX DX10 pixel oracles use an equivalent legacy masked DDS for FFmpeg, since this FFmpeg runtime also swaps R/B for those DX10 layouts. All six oracles are asserted equal to the authored pattern; actual DX10 headers remain in Rrrah inputs and transfer metadata is tested separately.

PCX corpus entries are copied from the existing CC0 fixtures and decoded with Pillow by `scripts/generate-pcx-corpus.py`.

For odd-width RGB PCX, Pillow readback misaligns padded planes. Its encoded file is verified using FFmpeg and the authored RGB pattern. Indexed PCX uses Pillow; both oracles are checked against the original pattern.

AVIF fixtures come from Pillow/libavif via `scripts/generate-avif-fixtures.py`. RGB and alpha+ICC cases use 4:4:4 quality 100, with three levels of decoder rounding tolerance; alpha is checked separately after display preparation.

Seven rectangular AVIF orientation fixtures are generated by `scripts/generate-avif-orientation-fixtures.py`. libavif converts EXIF orientation into irot/imir; Pillow reads stored pixels and its EXIF transpose supplies the oracle.

XBM X11 odd-width monochrome fixture is encoded by Pillow and decoded by FFmpeg with black foreground/white background by `scripts/generate-xbm-fixtures.py`. X10 shorts have separate synthetic padding/bit-order checks.

XPM fixture generated by `scripts/generate-xpm-fixtures.py` exercises two-character keys and transparent None; the oracle comes from FFmpeg, checked against the authored pixels.

SVG shapes/alpha/transform fixture uses CairoSVG and Pillow as independent oracle, generated by `scripts/generate-svg-fixtures.py`. One level of rounding tolerance is allowed.

Embedded SVG PNG alpha/vector fixture comes from `scripts/generate-svg-image-fixtures.py`, using a CairoSVG/Pillow oracle.

ORA fixtures are generated by `scripts/generate-ora-fixtures.py` using Python zipfile; Pillow decoding of the merged PNG supplies the oracle. Plain RGBA and ICC PNG are covered.

JPEG XL fixtures use libjxl cjxl/djxl 0.12.0 and Pillow via `scripts/generate-jxl-fixtures.py`: naked codestream and container preserve RGB/alpha with exact pixel oracles. A separate 16-bit grayscale fixture checks adjacent authored values 32768/32769 without quantization. All inputs are synthetic CC0.

JPEG 2000 fixtures use OpenJPEG 2.5.4 encoding and FFmpeg decoding through `scripts/generate-jp2-fixtures.py`. JP2 and bare J2K cover RGB/gray, JP2 covers straight alpha and inserted RGB ICC. Separate authored adjacent 16-bit samples check precision. Synthetic inputs are CC0.

DCX two-page indexed fixture uses independently encoded Pillow PCX pages and Pillow DCX page decoding; both page oracles are tested through the public API. Generator: `scripts/generate-dcx-fixtures.py`; synthetic CC0.

PSD/PSB synthetic compositions come from `scripts/generate-psd-fixtures.py`: FFmpeg supplies PSD raw/RLE oracles, psd-tools supplies PSB raw/RLE and RGB8 merged-transparency oracles. Adjacent 16-bit and float values have separate authored precision checks. CC0.

Photoshop ZIP and ZIP-prediction fixtures also use psd-tools oracles; its independent prediction encoder supplies authored 16-bit and float fixtures. The Rust tests reject truncated ZIP and trailing stream data.

KRA synthetic containers use `scripts/generate-kra-fixtures.py`; Python ZIP/Pillow decoding of the saved PNG supplies the pixel oracle. Plain RGBA and RGB ICC compositions include a Krita-style DOCTYPE. These are composition/container fixtures, not native Krita layer/tile acceptance files. CC0.

Alias PIX row-run fixtures use `scripts/generate-pix-fixtures.py`; independent FFmpeg alias_pix decoding supplies exact RGBA oracles for 8-bit gray and 24-bit BGR. Synthetic CC0.

IFF ILBM/PBM fixtures use `scripts/generate-iff-fixtures.py` and independent FFmpeg pixel/alpha oracles. Eleven fixtures cover odd-width row padding, raw/ByteRun1, transparent palette index, explicit mask plane, 24-bit RGB and EHB. Synthetic CC0.

Three HAM6 fixtures exercise palette and all component updates, row reset and transparency. FFmpeg provides RGB references. HAM alpha is authored directly from source mask/index values because FFmpeg loses mask-plane alpha; the test still compares all RGBA bytes exactly.

PKM fixtures use `scripts/generate-pkm-fixtures.py`, which compiles the independent Apache-2.0 Android ETC1 C++ decoder in a temporary directory. Source SHA256 is pinned in the script. ETC1 individual/differential and cropped multi-block RGB are covered, plus ETC2 compatible/opaque color and authored constant alpha. Broader ETC2 modes are not qualified by these files. All input textures are synthetic CC0.

KTX1 fixtures use `scripts/generate-ktx-fixtures.py`. Authored Pillow RGB/RGBA pixels cover both header byte orders, four orientations and row padding; BC1/2/3 payloads reuse independent DDS pixel oracles. Separate authored fixtures preserve 16-bit and float32 values in both byte orders. These do not constitute independent libktx/viewer interoperability proof. CC0.

HEIF/HEIC fixtures use `scripts/generate-heif-fixtures.py`: libheif 1.23.5/x265 lossless RGB encoding, authored Pillow source/rotation/mirror/straight-alpha references, and a secondary heif-convert check. Four RGBA8 corpus files and one adjacent 12-bit precision file are covered. The secondary decoder uses the same native library; independent HEVC codec comparison remains pending. Synthetic CC0.

ASTC fixtures use `scripts/generate-astc-fixtures.py <astcenc-path>` with Arm astcenc 4.6.1. Fourteen RGBA PNG oracles cover every standard 2D footprint with cropped 23x17 alpha-bearing surfaces. A separate HDR texture has an RGBA32F oracle extracted by OpenEXR 3.5.2 from astcenc EXR output. All authored inputs are synthetic CC0. The native library bundles astcenc 5.3.0; this compares reference implementations across versions rather than independent ASTC codecs.

KTX2 fixtures use `scripts/generate-ktx2-fixtures.py`. Twelve authored Pillow RGBA8 oracles cover four orientations, plain/DEFLATE, RGB/BGR/BGRA and two mips; four separate files check native 16-bit and float32 precision. DFD fields follow Khronos' canonical RGBSDA construction; compression uses Python zlib. These are synthetic CC0 fixtures, not independent libktx interoperability files.

`precision-manifest.tsv` contains sixteen additional typed u8/u16/f32 oracles, generated with `scripts/generate-precision-raster-fixtures.py` (numpy/OpenEXR 3.5.2). PAM/farbfeld/RGBE expected values are authored from format sample semantics; OpenEXR supplies independent HALF/FLOAT scanline NONE/RLE/ZIP/PIZ encoding/readback. EXR oracles convert stored associated RGB to the common straight-alpha API, preserving exact authored values. A separate legal zero-alpha emission EXR tests explicit rejection until associated-alpha rendering is implemented. All inputs are synthetic CC0.

Eight EXR composition oracles (`*.exr.over-rgb-f32`) are generated directly from OpenEXR readback of stored associated RGB and alpha over a linear RGB background (0.25, 0.5, 0.75), before any unassociation. The public decoder's straight RGB/alpha must reconstruct that reference composition sample-for-sample for HALF/FLOAT and NONE/RLE/ZIP/PIZ. This verifies composition equivalence at the library boundary, not GPU/window display or zero-alpha emission support.

MacPaint data-fork fixtures use `scripts/generate-macpaint-fixtures.py`. Netpbm 11.02.30 macptopbm supplies independent PBM decode, then Pillow converts to exact RGBA8. Four files cover versions 0/2, custom pattern tables, literals and mixed repeat/literal/no-op rows with full 576x720 coordinate patterns. Synthetic CC0; wrapper/native-app qualification remains pending.

Netpbm macptopbm 11.02.30 interprets PackBits -128 as repeat-129 instead of no-op. For mixed fixtures, the generator therefore decodes an independently valid equivalent stream without the inserted no-op controls, and uses those pixels as the expected result. No-op identity also has a direct authored unit check. Literal fixture oracles decode the source files directly. This is not direct Netpbm interoperability proof for no-op-bearing streams.

Six MacBinary fixtures extend `generate-macpaint-fixtures.py`: I/II/III wrappers, each with/without a resource fork, use Netpbm's independent wrapper detection and pixel decoding. Python binascii.crc_hqx generates II/III header checksums; Rust also checks the standard CRC vector. Bounds/padding/CRC corruption and misleading RAW-extension routing have explicit tests. Secondary-header rounding is authored structural evidence, not native wrapper interoperability proof. Synthetic CC0.

WAL fixtures use `scripts/generate-wal-fixtures.py`: two CC0 indexed mip chains, an authored RGBA palette and indexed PCX colormap. Pillow's explicit WAL parser with palette override supplies exact RGBA oracles. `wal-manifest.tsv` stores name, width, height, oracle and source SHA-256. No game palette assets are bundled.

DPX fixtures use `scripts/generate-dpx-fixtures.py`: 24 authored CC0 single-element files covering both endian orders, 8/10/12/16-bit samples, RGB/RGBA/ABGR/luma and packed/filled A/B subsets. FFmpeg native-depth readback supplies independent sample oracles; 10/12-bit values are normalized to full 16-bit with rounding. `dpx-manifest.tsv` stores name, width, height, sample kind, oracle and source SHA-256. Undefined transfer/color fields deliberately remain unspecified. Orientation, nonzero line/image padding, linear reference metadata and ABGR16 have separate authored unit checks.

Cineon fixtures use `scripts/generate-cineon-fixtures.py` with OpenImageIO 3.2.1.1 and OpenEXR Python readback. Twelve authored CC0 V4.5 files cover gray/RGB 8/16-bit and RGB 10-bit longword-left/right, in both endian orders. The native reader's recovered sample codes are normalized to the library's full-range representation without a color transform. `cineon-manifest.tsv` stores name, width, height, kind, oracle and source SHA-256. Film-log display is not covered.

Softimage PIC fixtures use `scripts/generate-softimage-fixtures.py`: 12 CC0 RGB/RGBA cases in raw, pure-RLE and mixed-RLE storage, including 8/16-bit and mixed-depth packets, 16-bit alpha and extended repeats. OpenImageIO 3.2.1.1 readback with `--no-autopremult` supplies independent exact sample oracles through float EXR. `softimage-manifest.tsv` stores name, dimensions, kind, oracle and source SHA-256.

Wavefront RLA fixtures use `scripts/generate-rla-fixtures.py`: 14 authored CC0 indexed gray/RGB records, optional alpha, 8/16-bit and mixed group depth, negative literal/positive repeated byte-plane RLE, and deliberately reordered physical scanlines. OpenImageIO 3.2.1.1 float EXR readback supplies independent stored-sample oracles. Gray/matte channel names are R/G in that writer, so the generator explicitly maps them to gray/alpha. `rla-manifest.tsv` stores name, dimensions, kind, oracle and source SHA-256. Alpha association is supplied by the test, not inferred from the file.

WAD3 fixtures use `scripts/generate-wad-fixtures.py` with vgio 1.3.0 and Pillow. Two authored CC0 archives each contain a service record, an opaque 16x16 texture and a cutout 32x16 texture, with all four mips and per-texture palettes; physical texture ordering differs. `wad-manifest.tsv` stores archive, selected image index, width, height, oracle and source SHA-256. vgio independently parses directory/mip indices, while the palette and index-255 cutout rule are authored expectations; this is not a complete independent WAD3/GoldSrc engine oracle.

NRRD fixtures use `scripts/generate-nrrd-fixtures.py` with pynrrd 1.1.3 and NumPy. Sixteen authored CC0 scalar volumes contain 32 selected planes covering uint8/uint16/int16/float32, raw/gzip/text, both binary endian orders, signed extremes and adjacent float values. pynrrd readback supplies exact float32 raw-unit RGBA oracles with opaque alpha. `nrrd-manifest.tsv` stores source, selected plane, dimensions, oracle and SHA-256. Header comments omit generation time for reproducibility. Explicit display windows and malformed/nonfinite cases have separate authored tests.

MRC fixtures use `scripts/generate-mrc-fixtures.py` with mrcfile 1.5.4 and NumPy. Ten authored CC0 volumes provide 20 exact raw-unit plane oracles for signed 8/16-bit, unsigned 16-bit, float16/32 and both byte orders. Physical axes are deliberately permuted; raw extended-header bytes and nonzero origins are retained. Big-endian signed-8 header authoring uses NumPy's structured header byte conversion because mrcfile otherwise uses native byte order for byte samples. Independent mrcfile readback validates every source. `mrc-manifest.tsv` stores source, selected plane, dimensions, oracle and SHA-256. NumPy also supplies all 65,536 half-to-float conversion results, including signed zeros, denormals, infinities and quieted signaling NaNs.

FITS fixtures use `scripts/generate-fits-fixtures.py` with Astropy 7.2.0 and NumPy. Eleven authored CC0 files provide 22 selected planes with native byte oracles, physical float64 values and explicit-window float32 RGBA (-100..1000). They cover unsigned 8/16-bit, signed 16/32/64-bit, IEEE float32/64, negative BSCALE, BZERO, BLANK, nonfinite samples, empty primary, IMAGE HDUs and a heap-bearing binary table between images. Native readback disables scaling; physical readback independently enables Astropy scaling. Original WCS/units, quoted slash/apostrophe strings and repeated HISTORY are authored. `fits-manifest.tsv` stores source, index, dimensions, native type, three oracles and source SHA-256. NaN/infinity/BLANK planes require a separate missing-value policy and are rejected by ordinary windowing. Extreme integer offset cancellation has a separate exact authored regression; no Astropy precision guarantee is inferred for that case.

PVR v3 fixtures use `scripts/generate-pvr-fixtures.py`: eighteen authored CC0 files provide 58 selected-mip native-byte oracles. Ordinary normalized 8/16-bit and float32 descriptors cover both byte orders, channel ordering, luminance/alpha, sparse channels, orientation and uniform metadata type override. NumPy authors these sample expectations; they are not independent PVR container-reader evidence. Three linear-premultiplied fixtures also supply composition oracles over RGB (0.25, 0.5, 0.75).

PVRTC1 RGB/RGBA 2/4-bpp payloads use standard-library `random.Random(8741)` and are independently decoded by the MIT PowerVR Native SDK raw-block decompressor at revision `63f0098acdc11ec9a072c30000d2fa670a955bee`. The generator verifies SHA-256 of `PVRTDecompress.cpp` (`74559c5a4b8161aafce1ebe984bf8060896feaa81276b614491dbee755d6e4c7`), its header (`67123a36b99df380af76a65f3dfa3a7f368a153f5401b36a9ff1ed233cee6f5f`) and SDK license (`b1aea79afab593649ede742eccbb7feb74d216d52d120b99c4d349133871ba9f`). Source and license are cached externally in a temporary directory; no vendor image assets or runtime C++ dependency are added. `scripts/pvr-fixture-oracle.cpp` wraps only raw block decoding. Container fields, orientation and the RGB opaque-alpha rule remain authored expectations, not independent full PVR-loader qualification.

`pvr-manifest.tsv` stores source, selected mip, dimensions, sample kind, transfer declaration, native oracle, optional composition oracle and source SHA-256. All 58 oracle lengths and source hashes were checked; a second generation produced identical bytes. Legacy PVR, other compressed codecs, cube/array/volume textures and live viewer qualification remain pending.

DDS 2D mip-chain fixtures use `scripts/generate-dds-mip-fixtures.py`. Nine authored CC0 chains target 36 selected mips (9x5, 4x2, 2x1, 1x1): legacy BC1/2/3, DX10 BC1 sRGB/BC3 linear, RGB565, RGB24, BGRA32 and DX10 RGBA32 sRGB. Pillow independently decodes a standalone container for each authored payload (BC1 sRGB uses an equivalent UNORM header for raw-sample readback because Pillow lacks that sRGB enum); this validates selected-level samples, not independent interpretation of full-chain offsets. `dds-mip-manifest.tsv` records source, level, dimensions, transfer, oracle and source SHA-256. Full-chain interoperability and padded uncompressed mip layout remain pending.

KTX1 selected-mip fixtures use `scripts/generate-ktx-mip-fixtures.py`: fifteen authored CC0 chains provide sixty native-byte oracles at 9x5, 4x2, 2x1 and 1x1. Twelve ordinary RGB/RGBA chains cover 8/16/float32 samples, both byte orders, row padding and X/Y orientation. Python struct authors their native sample expectations, including negative/HDR RGB and fractional alpha. Three BC1/2/3 chains reuse raw DDS mip payloads and their independent Pillow pixel oracles; compressed bytes retain their order even in the big-endian BC2 container. These verify sample/selection contracts, not independent full KTX loader interoperability. `ktx-mip-manifest.tsv` stores source, level, dimensions, kind, transfer, oracle and source SHA-256. All hashes and oracle lengths were checked; regeneration produced identical bytes.

KTX2 selected-mip fixtures use `scripts/generate-ktx2-mip-fixtures.py` and the shared existing KTX2 container builder. Twenty-four authored CC0 chains provide 96 native-byte oracles for RGB/BGRA8, RGB(A)16/float32, ordinary/DEFLATE, rd/lu orientation and four stored mips. Lower mips are physically stored before the base level. Native samples are authored with Python struct; compression uses zlib. These are contract fixtures, not independent libktx decoding evidence. `ktx2-mip-manifest.tsv` records source, selection, dimensions, kind, transfer, oracle and source SHA-256. Hashes/lengths and byte-identical regeneration were verified.

APNG fixtures use `scripts/generate-apng-fixtures.py`: three authored CC0 streams provide twelve authored linear-light float32 presentation oracles, plus independent FFmpeg 9.0.2 compatibility-frame readback (`*.compat-rgba`). Four-frame 5x3 animations cover SOURCE/OVER, partial rectangles, fractional alpha, NONE/BACKGROUND/PREVIOUS disposal, rational/zero delays, denominator-zero normalization, finite/infinite loops and a separate default image outside the animation. Chunk structure/CRC/controls and linear compositing expectations are authored with Python struct/zlib/float64 arithmetic. FFmpeg decodes full animations with ignore_loop=1 and passthrough timing, excluding separate previews. Its encoded-space OVER samples are not a color-correct linear-light oracle.

Pillow APNG OVER readback produced alpha 191 over an opaque destination; image crate APNG readback produced 254. The library uses still-PNG decoding, existing color preparation and its own linear float compositor. Both it and the linear reference preserve alpha 1 over opaque backgrounds; FFmpeg also preserves encoded alpha 255. `apng-manifest.tsv` records source, index, dimensions, millisecond delay ratio, num_plays, linear oracle and source SHA-256. Live timed playback, wider/palette/interlaced variants, 16-bit compositing, unqualified source colors and animated EXIF orientation remain pending.

GIF animation fixtures are authored CC0 by `scripts/generate-gif-animation-fixtures.py`, with independent Pillow RGBA presentation readback. Three 5x3 animations cover partial frames and KEEP/BACKGROUND/PREVIOUS disposal, transparent index, delays including zero and finite repetition; twelve selections are recorded in `gif-animation-manifest.tsv`. Logical-background/color-extension variants and live timed playback remain unqualified.

Animated WebP CC0 fixtures are generated by `scripts/generate-webp-animation-fixtures.py`: four authored containers, sixteen float32 presentation oracles. libwebp cwebp/dwebp independently encodes/reads raw frames (lossless VP8L and lossy VP8+ALPH), and Python float64 linear-light equations define composition expectations. Partial rectangles, SOURCE/OVER, background disposal, transparent/partly transparent background, zero delays and zero/finite plays are covered. `webp-animation-manifest.tsv` retains source hashes and selected metadata. This is not independent full-animation color interoperability.

JNG fixtures are authored CC0 by `scripts/generate-jng-fixtures.py`: eight standalone containers, Pillow JPEG color/JPEG-alpha sample readback and authored lossless 1/2/4/8/16-bit alpha. `jng-manifest.tsv` records RGBA16 oracle samples and source hashes. JPEG RGB/JPEG alpha permit two 8-bit levels of independent decoder rounding; lossless alpha is exact, including adjacent 16-bit values. Full independent JNG-loader interoperability remains pending.

JPEG-LS CC0 samples come from `scripts/generate-jpegls-fixtures.py`: 29 gray/RGB files, six depths (2/4/8/10/12/16), planar/line/sample layout and lossless/near-lossless. Three files are FFmpeg-encoded; a test-only CharLS encoder produces the others. Thirteen oracles use independent FFmpeg readback, sixteen use exact authored lossless source samples because FFmpeg RGB precision/sample-interleave readback is unqualified. Source gray samples are shifted back from FFmpeg storage alignment, then expanded injectively to RGBA8/16 full range. `jpegls-manifest.tsv` distinguishes oracle provenance, retains NEAR/layout/depth and hashes. Native decode and encoder share CharLS in authored cases; these are not independent interoperability proof.

JPEG-XR: `generate-jpegxr-fixtures.py` authors 21 CC0 files and typed RGBA8/16/float32 oracles. JXRLib 1.1 encodes the source arrays; independent openreadout-jpegxr 0.1.0 verifies non-alpha native samples. Orientation is an authored transform, explicitly identified in the manifest. Alpha is checked with shared JXRLib readback; integer source samples additionally round-trip exactly. The generator builds the checked-in standalone Rust helper in a temporary project (Rust >=1.91), without changing the runtime workspace MSRV/dependencies. Canonical and legacy absolute-end alpha-count files are both present.

Aseprite: `generate-aseprite-fixtures.py` creates 21 CC0 RGBA/gray-alpha/indexed files and 63 selected-frame oracles: 39 independently read with asefile 0.3.8, 24 authored source/composition contracts. The checked-in standalone Rust helper is built in a temporary project, not added to runtime dependencies. Raw/zlib storage, links, clipping, legacy/modern palettes and native normal blending are covered. Old opacity-validity flags, moving/forward/chained links, palette changes, groups and ICC/linear gamma exceed the reference decoder's qualified behavior, so their provenance remains authored. The manifest records selection, timing/counts, provenance, oracle path and source SHA256; the Rust tests retain tag and layer metadata as well.
